newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Thorn H1 profits seen rising.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Thorn H1 profits seen rising.

text.p: UK electrical giant Thorn Plc, recently divorced from its long-term partner EMI, is seen posting a moderate rise in interim profits on Monday thanks to higher sales in its non-British markets, analysts said.
They expect the company to report a pre-tax profit of around 78 million stg, up from 71.5 million last year.
"The results will not be very exciting compared to other retailers but it (the profit rise) will be fairly decent," said analyst Nick Bubb of Mees Pierson.
Turnover is seen ranging between 790 and 800 million stg.
Analysts said Thorn's turnover from its British business could see a decline of around five percent but it would make up through a growth of 18 percent or so in business in the U.S.
"The first quarter trends should continue into the second," said Victoria Melendez, analyst with Morgan Stanley.
In the first quarter to June, 38 percent of Thorn's sales came from the United States, 30 percent from Britain, 28 percent from mainland Europe with the rest from the Asia Pacific region.
"Overall, we are looking at a 10 percent rise in sales," said Melendez.

While legal battles regarding rental purchase transactions in the United States would continue to affect share price sentiments, its sales have been boosted through two franchise acquisitions in that country, analysts said.
"A sales boost is also seen in the Nordic region," Melendez said.
Analysts said the company may seem less glamorous than the combined Thorn-EMI, but it will continue to thrive on its innovative consumer-friendly techniques.
For example, Thorn has been offering easy, cheap rental schemes to consumers at France's Crazy George chain, the publicity for which provoked the French government's wrath.
"The Crazy George stuff will bring in growth," said Bubb.
Analysts had valued Thorn's share at between 390 and 420p at the time of its demerger from EMI Group, but it has fallen to 346p.
Most analysts, however, see a gradual emergence of buying interest in Thorn on estimates that it would complete its full year with growth of between 11 and 12 percent.
